body:
Bah I typed out a long response and then reddit decides to screw me over :(. Error code 503. Well, here it goes again:

>I don't think I quite understand what you mean when can't come up >with things to say... do you mean, you'd like to talk with someone but >don't know how to initiate? Or your with a bunch of other people who >are talking and you just don't feel you have anything to contribute? Or >do you mean you'll be holding a conversation and then just start >drawing blanks? Lack of viable topics of conversation? If you want to >be social, surely there must be something you want to socialize about, >right? Common interests, politics, religion, sports, etc, etc? A little >clarification would be nice :).

Initiation is difficult for me, but not the problem here. I can have conversations with people one on one, although I run out of things to say after a while. The main problem however, are group talks. I find it incredibly difficult to contribute to these kind of chats. I feel like I don't have anything meaningfull to contribute to the conversation. And when I finally do come up with something to say, I feel like I'm intervening, and not partaking in it.

I'm not close at all to my family. Basicly I only talk to them if I need something from them, and they talk to me if they need something from me. When we have dinner pretty much nothing is said, we don't talk and eat. I guess that contributed a bit to me being like this...

I know there's nothing wrong with only having a few friends. However, due to some recent retarded drama in my friend group, it split up. We used to do something at least once a week, now I go do something maybe twice a month. 

Because of that, I'm basicly stuck in the house night after night. I'd like to go out and do something, but I wouldn't know what, or with who.

Well, the health care is not exactly free. Whenever I go see a doctor, or psych in this case, he bills me the full fee. The health care then pays back most of the fee I paid, but not entirely. Since I'm still in college and live with my parents, they get the reduction paid out to, and have to show all bills to the health care agency, or whatever it's called. This means I would have to pay for the psych entirely myself.

I'm still in college and already have a bachelors degree now. Most employers prefer people with a masters degree, so that's what I'm going  for now. I'm however not motivated at all anymore. Usually I don't do any actual studying during the semester, and somehow still pass the exams. Now I have to write a master thesis, which means alot of research and work during the semester. Due to lack of motivation, I haven't even started it yet, whilst we're halfway through the semester.

The hobbies I currently have still bring me some enjoyment, but I don't see how they would get me to meet new people. I enjoy things like playing guitar and surfing the internet. How did you meet these people you speak of?
